title: Host-task agent routing ignores NexusLoop production_mode (router built with default False)
impact: NexusLoop passes its production_mode to its own AgentRouter, but build_host_task_execution() constructs a second AgentRouter without it (default False). HostTaskExecution.execute routes through that router whenever task.agent_id is empty, so the production-only checks (lifecycle state must be production/staging; owner and runbook metadata for production-eligible agents) are skipped on the canonical host-task path even for a production-mode loop. NexusLoop.production_mode also defaults to False whereas RuntimeConfig.production_mode defaults to True. Code behavior confirmed by reading; reachability from a production host with an empty agent_id was not executed.
recommendation: Pass the loop's production_mode (or a typed routing-policy object) into the host-task router, add a negative test asserting a non-production-state agent is rejected on the host-task path in production mode, and align the NexusLoop default with RuntimeConfig.

title: AgentRouter silently falls back to the first routable agent (undocumented, untested)
affected_invariant: No unauthorized fallbacks / FRZ-OWN-04 no shadow authority
evidence: E1:grep fallback_first_routable over docs/ and tests/ at BASELINE returned 0 hits
impact: When neither explicit agent_id, capability match nor best match resolves, _route_best_or_fallback selects list_routable_agent_ids()[0] and marks fallback_used=True. The choice is observable via the AGENT_SELECTED event but is not described in ORCHESTRATION/NEXUS docs nor asserted by any test found, so a task can execute on an arbitrary agent instead of failing closed.
recommendation: Document the fallback as an explicit policy or remove it (fail closed); add a test for the no-match case.

title: Governance and routing strictness depend on production_mode/non-strict flags; three Tier-2 agents build RuntimeContext directly with relaxed settings (reachability unproven)
affected_invariant: FRZ-GOV-05 fresh authorization before meaningful effects; FRZ-BND-05 construction only via sanctioned composition
impact: Code shows: non-strict hosts get authorization_port=None and no agent runtime governance; harness_production_mode() is hard-coded False; agents/external_contractor_adapter and organization_worker build their own RuntimeContext with production_mode False, and the flag defaults differ across modules (RuntimeConfig True; NexusLoop, AgentRouter, emit_context False). Whether any production-qualified host can reach these paths is not established, and the architecture docs mention production_mode in only a handful of places. Evidence for the code facts is E3; the risk claim itself is a hypothesis.
recommendation: Campaign B: enumerate every host/agent path that reaches RuntimeContext.build with production_mode False and prove it is lab/test only; document the flag contract in PLATFORM_FOUNDATION or GOVERNED_EXECUTION.
